results.fact: Gain vs loss on an out-and-back
results.evidence: Gain of 4,000 ft is confirmed again (WTA hike page: 4,000 ft gain). No page found states a car-to-car descent figure: the Country Highpoints survey and winter-ascent reports, WTA and the Mazamas give no loss figure, and the Mountaineers route page is blocked. Under the loss_ft rule loss_ft stays. Would settle: a GPS track or route page stating the round-trip descent for the Willow Creek line.

New figures for the Rainy Pass - Wing Lake - South Ridge round trip still disagree: the FKT route page gives 11.5 mi and 5,000 ft; The Outbound gives 4,700 ft over 7 mi; earlier found Hiiker ~5,577, Willhite 4,500 ft. All exceed the stored 3,971 ft, but no two independent sources agree on one value, and none states a car-to-car loss. Would settle: two sources (e.g. GPS tracks) agreeing on one car-to-car gain.

results.fact: Where to leave the trail for the col
results.correct_value: Leave the trail at Shellrock Pass itself (~7,500 ft), as the approach text and the col waypoint already say; Eureka Creek lies on the approach side before Shellrock Basin, and the far side of the pass descends into the North Monument Creek basin.
results.evidence: Four independent trip reports go up to Shellrock Pass and head for Blackcap from there: trailcatjim (hiked up to Shellrock Pass, then traversed over to Blackcap; order is Eureka Creek, then Shellrock Basin, then the pass), Mountain Flamingo (followed the trail up to Shellrock Pass, dropped gear on the ridge), Hike2Hike (bivied just below the pass, climbed from the pass along the ridge), Country Highpoints (ridge southwest from Shellrock Pass to the col). trailcatjim's Lost Peak loop confirms the far side of the pass drops into North Monument Creek basin, not Eureka Creek. The variant's 7,100 ft leave-point and 'over the pass into Eureka Creek' are the outliers.

patches.fact: Where to leave the trail for the col
patches.find: Leave the trail at about 7,100 ft, just before the steep switchbacks that climb to Shellrock Pass, and traverse
patches.replace: Leave the trail at Shellrock Pass itself and traverse

patches.fact: Where to leave the trail for the col
patches.find: Crossing Shellrock Pass itself and dropping over the far side puts you into Eureka Creek, well north of anything you want.
patches.replace: Following the trail over Shellrock Pass and down its far side takes you away from the peak altogether.

results.fact: dist_km holds the round trip, not the one-way approach
results.evidence: Still no page states a one-way Slate Pass-to-Blackcap distance. Country Highpoints used the Monument Creek trailhead and gives no Slate Pass mileage; Mountain Flamingo gives only a 62 mi multi-peak total; a WTA trip report gives ~8 mi from the Middle Fork turnoff to Shellrock Pass, which would need to be summed with other segments (not allowed). Would settle: a source stating the one-way trailhead-to-summit mileage.

results.fact: Parking pass at the Slate Pass trailhead
results.evidence: Sources disagree. WTA's Buckskin Ridge page, at the very coordinates of this row's trailhead pin (48.7323, -120.6683), lists a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass. The Forest Service Slate Pass Trailhead page says 'No fees required', and WTA's Whistler Cutoff page says none. The row's note is left as it is. Would settle: the Methow Valley Ranger District confirming whether the Slate Pass trailhead is a fee site.

gain_ft/loss_ft 4,571 is clearly far too small for the 64 mi Harts Pass round trip, but still no page states a car-to-car gain for the Harts Pass-PCT-Castle Pass-Frosty Pass line. The only stated total is trailcatjim's 13,000 ft over 39.3 mi from Manning Park, a different route that is no longer a lawful way in. PCT section pages give no cumulative gain to Castle Pass. Would settle: two GPS tracks or route pages giving the Harts Pass round-trip gain.

No new timing to the col was found. Peak of the Week gives the col at 7,720 ft but no time; Climber Kyle (~13 h, a linkup) and Francis Bailey (14 h 27 min car-to-car) give only totals; a SummitPost summary gives 2-4 h trailhead to camp. The row's 2.5 h, 3-4 h and 4-6 h still lack two sources that agree. Would settle: two trip reports timing car-to-col.

Four copies in the row say 8,400 ft (high_point_ft, the summit waypoint elev and elevFt, and the schedule's 'Summit (8,400 ft)'); only the itinerary objective says 8,483. SummitPost gives 2,560 m (~8,400 ft), and search listings for the Peakbagger page also show 8,400 ft. No source gives 8,483; Lists of John gives a lidar figure of 8,492 ft, so if that is ever adopted all copies must move together. The single outlier is aligned to the row's published figure. (USGS point elevation at the summit pin reads ~8,167 ft, i.e. the pin is off the narrow summit and does not decide this.)
